plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: Glossy evergreen shrubs light up the cold-season woodlands of coastal Japan with satin-textured, rose-like blooms. Each flower sits close along the branch, with a bright boss of golden stamens at its center. The petals stand out vividly against dark, leathery leaves.
plants.bloomingSeason: Wild plants flower from about January to March, so mid-January is the start of the show.
plants.location: Coastal woodlands and gardens of Japan, and temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Camellia japonica is a close relative of the tea plant, Camellia sinensis. In Japan, camellia oil pressed from its seeds has long been used for hair and skin care.

plants.name: Hamamelis x intermedia
plants.description: On bare winter branches, witch hazel unfurls spidery, ribbon-like petals that crinkle and curl like confetti. The flowers glow in fiery shades against the grey landscape, and many carry a spicy fragrance. They bring color and scent to the quietest part of the garden year.
plants.bloomingSeason: Some start in late December or early January, and bloom peaks from mid-January to mid-March.
plants.location: Temperate gardens of North America and Europe, such as the Missouri Botanical Garden in the USA
plants.funFact: The petals curl up tightly in freezing weather and unfurl again when it warms, which helps protect the flowers from frost damage.

plants.name: Agapanthus africanus
plants.description: Rounded clusters of bell-shaped, violet-blue flowers rise on slender stalks above arching, strap-like leaves. On the sunny slopes of the southwestern Cape, they bring a splash of cool color to the height of the southern summer.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer in the Southern Hemisphere, including January, when it has been recorded in flower on Table Mountain.
plants.location: Table Mountain and the Cape region of South Africa
plants.funFact: Despite the common name, it is not a true lily. Its name comes from the Greek words for love and flower, and it is a cherished garden plant around the world.
